public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI agents are not autonomous, do not replace jobs or coders, and will not do so, because probabilistic models are poor at taking precise actions.

statement.excerpt: Long story short, agents are not autonomous, they do not replace jobs, they cannot “replace coders,” they are not going to do so because probabilistic models are a horrible means of taking precise actions, and almost anyone who brings up agents as a booster is either misinformed or in the business of misinformation.

our_interpretation: Assess the forecast about LLM agents replacing jobs, including software-development jobs. The present-tense assertions and proposed technical explanation inform its meaning.
The surrounding passage defines autonomy as doing an entire job. I therefore distinguish sustained performance of a job's substantive responsibilities from completing individual tasks.
Replacement can include eliminating positions, foregoing identifiable hires, or transferring their responsibilities to agents while reassigning employees. It need not mean dismissing workers.
No numerical scale or deadline is supplied. A well-documented deployment could disprove the categorical forecast without an economy-wide employment decline.
The statement about boosters' motives is not part of the checkable forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence would need to establish a durable barrier preventing the specified job replacement. Present failures or continued human employment cannot establish that replacement will never happen.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented deployment shows LLM agents reliably performing the substantive responsibilities of identifiable jobs with sufficiently limited human intervention to replace those positions or their staffing requirements.

evidence.explanation: Anthropic describes a product-content team transferring work to agents and moving into prompting and evaluations in spring 2026. This challenges the broad denial of replacement, but does not establish how independently the agents perform the complete former roles.

The research measures success on bounded tasks and discusses substantial measurement uncertainty. Those results do not directly measure job replacement or establish a permanent inability to perform precise work.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated deployment record documenting the former job, responsibilities assumed by agents, sustained quality, human intervention, and resulting staffing replacement would permit contradiction.
